S.name: Twin of the exact target, scoped to the task
S.detail: The twin reconstructs the specific deployment environment restricted to the task-relevant subset, with pruned regions as explicit placeholders; a twin of the exact target scene beats generic assets (90% vs 10% real success) (2403.03949#s1, 2609.07712#s1).

S.name: Resettable to logged real states
S.detail: The simulator can be reset to recorded real states and real states are measurable, so simulated and real next states can be compared step by step (2502.01143#s1, 2402.01086#s1).

S.name: Twin preserves real ranking
S.detail: Offline twin evaluation is shown to preserve the relative ordering of checkpoints/agents seen in the real environment (reported with 5-8x speedup) (2504.03597#s1).

S.name: Real data kept in the training mixture
S.detail: Distillation or retraining co-trains on real demonstrations (3.5x/2x over sim co-training); targeted twin demos are added where the policy fails (30 targeted sim demos ~= 30 extra real demos) (2403.03949#s3, 2504.03597#s2).

S.name: Correction model is more expressive than a global parameter fit
S.detail: A learned residual beats parameter SysID, which yields implausible parameters and little gain; debiasing uses context features that separate regions where the twin is wrong; RL fine-tuning in the corrected simulator beats training-free use of the correction (2402.01086#s2, 2502.01143#s1, 2507.07067#s3, 2502.01143#s2).

F.name: Training without real anchor
F.detail: Policies trained without real demos exploit twin inaccuracies; sim-only demos can include behaviour that breaks synchronisation at deployment (2403.03949#s1, 2504.03597#s2).

F.name: Fidelity measured only indirectly
F.detail: Behavioural fidelity is measured only indirectly (placeholder residual up to 20.6%); dynamic content, network, personalisation and long-tail data are omitted (2609.07712#s1, 2504.03597#s1).

F.name: Single global bias correction
F.detail: Plain PPI with a single global bias underperforms real-only training where the twin is wrong; calibration cannot fully remove the gap of a limited-complexity simulator (2507.07067#s3, 2507.07067#s1).

F.name: Correction evaluated out of its regime
F.detail: Out-of-distribution regimes (1.75x pressure) break the residual and autoregressive error accumulates; at short horizons it is not better than open-loop/SysID (2402.01086#s1, 2502.01143#s1).

F.name: Bootstrap needs the real policy to succeed in the twin
F.detail: Step-function dependence on demo count: 0% when the real policy fails in sim (2403.03949#s2).

F.name: Construction cost unreported or prohibitive
F.detail: ~2 days wall-clock per task; full 23-DoF delta model impractical (reduced to 4-DoF); Bayesian twin training costs more compute (2403.03949#s3, 2502.01143#s1, 2507.07067#s2).

S.name: Experience from the same environments
S.detail: Memory is built from the same applications/environments (self-supervised exploration on benchmark initial states) (2410.08164#s2).

S.name: Summaries rather than raw trajectories, with ablation
S.detail: Stored experience is summarised by a self-evaluator, and removing the summaries is ablated (26.15 -> 18.46) (2410.08164#s2).

S.name: Memory-size scaling reported
S.detail: Scaling with memory size is reported: continuous (Q-Former) memory scales log-linearly where text memory degrades beyond ~10 items (2510.09038#s1).

S.name: Hierarchical planning with retrieved knowledge
S.detail: A manager fuses web search and narrative memory into a subtask queue executed by workers, with replanning on failure; requires a proprietary MLLM, web search and an accessibility tree (2410.08164#s1).

F.name: Small out-of-distribution gain
F.detail: OOD gains are small (OSWorld 26.40 -> 26.73) and retrieval drifts under UI shifts (2510.09038#s1).

F.name: Self-evaluator / reflector not validated
F.detail: Self-evaluator correctness is unmeasured; reflector labels disagree with humans ~25% (2410.08164#s2, 2311.08649#s2).

F.name: Held-out environment gains not isolated
F.detail: Gains on environments other than those the memory was built from are not isolated (2410.08164#s2).

F.name: Thin ablations and execution-dominated failures
F.detail: Ablations on 65 tasks with a single run; execution errors account for 79.59% of failures (2410.08164#s1).

S.name: Interaction-first beats instruction-first at equal budget
S.detail: The paper compares exploration-first (hindsight) synthesis against instruction-first synthesis at equal budget (MiniWoB 0.48 vs 0.28; WebArena 7.2 vs 4.2) (2410.02907#s3).

S.name: Instructions reference explored, site-specific entities
S.detail: Synthesised instructions reference deep, site-specific entities discovered by exploration, relabelled by a strong LLM/VLM (2410.02907#s3, 2412.19723#s1, 2410.02907#s1).

S.name: Feasibility/difficulty filter on proposed tasks
S.detail: Proposed tasks are filtered by a feasibility or difficulty signal (activity lists, critic value band [0.05, 0.75], feasibility rules) (2311.08649#s1, 2411.02337#s1).

S.name: History presented per cluster, intents from memory
S.detail: Proposals are conditioned on history presented per cluster of the UI transition graph rather than the whole graph or recent states only (coverage 36.94 vs 26.09/31.51), with intents generated from stored history rather than the live screen (2609.10031#s1, 2609.10031#s2).

S.name: Failure-conditioned curriculum shown to transfer
S.detail: A self-evolving curriculum built from failed tasks improves online RL and transfers to another RL algorithm (DigiRL) (2411.02337#s1).

F.name: Synthesis environments overlap evaluation
F.detail: Synthesis environments overlap the evaluation environments (2412.19723#s1).

F.name: Poor cross-site transfer
F.detail: Synthesised data transfers poorly across sites; mixing live and WebArena data hurts 7 sites (2410.02907#s2).

F.name: Kept-trajectory judge precision unmeasured
F.detail: Judge precision for kept trajectories is not measured, and self-reinforcing loops may overfit easy/popular sites (2510.09038#s2).

F.name: Saturation bounded by the executor
F.detail: Gains saturate with scale, bounded by executor capability (2412.19723#s1).

F.name: Exploration blind spots
F.detail: Widgets without text and single views with sub-regions are poorly explored; live-site exploration cannot log in or submit content; mocked values from instrumentation may not initialise realistic state (2311.08649#s1, 2410.02907#s1, 2601.21253#s2, 2601.21253#s3).

F.name: Hand-written feasibility rules and noisy generation
F.detail: Task-generation randomness raises variance, feasibility rules are hand-written per environment, and residual duplicate or non-existent-functionality intents remain (2411.02337#s1, 2609.10031#s1).

S.name: Abstracted transition target
S.detail: The world model predicts an abstraction of the change (Hungarian-matched element diff rewritten in natural language, or a delta from a retrieved HTML of the same app) rather than the raw full next state; raw-tree targets drop downstream SR 22.0 -> 14.5, and retrieval-grounded delta generation scores 73.51 vs 67.46 without RAG (2410.13232#s1, 2608.05891#s1).

S.name: Transitions harvested from real execution
S.detail: Training transitions come from executing in real pages/apps (goal-free random or structured walks, deduplicated structurally and visually, e.g. MinHash plus pHash) and are captioned by a VLM, not imagined by a teacher (2604.02345#s1, 2411.06559#s2).

S.name: Short imagination horizon
S.detail: Imagined rollouts used for policy training are kept short (best 4-5 steps), with the horizon ablated (2601.22149#s2).

S.name: Real-data anchor in the training mixture
S.detail: Imagined trajectories are mixed with real expert or public trajectories (~40% real gives most of the gain), and the world model is fine-tuned on the target environment family (2601.22149#s2, 2608.05891#s3, 2602.14721#s2).

S.name: World-model reward is not visual-only
S.detail: When the world model is itself RL-trained, its reward combines visual alignment with an action-consequence (transition validity) judge; either alone is worse and visual-only reward is reward-hacked (2602.09856#s1).

S.name: Transition objective compared under matched data
S.detail: A forward-dynamics pretraining objective is compared against inverse/backward variants with identical post-training data (EM 53.9/54.4 vs 51.0 baseline); explicit auxiliary tasks restore verification/reversal ability eroded by regular GUI pretraining (87.56 verification, 93.81 reversal) (2604.02345#s3, 2604.02345#s2, 2506.08012#s3).

F.name: Policy trained on imagination alone
F.detail: Purely imagined training underperforms SFT or lowers ATP below the base model (2601.22149#s2, 2608.05891#s3).

F.name: Long dreams or full-page prediction
F.detail: Long dreams degrade through compounding hallucination and only ~1/10 world-model rollouts pass quality checks; full-page transitions are much harder (~12% completely wrong) (2601.22149#s2, 2608.05891#s3, 2601.22149#s1).

F.name: Next state depends on hidden server state
F.detail: The model has no access to server-side state, real assets or pixels by construction; counterfactual imagination accounts for 42% of sampled errors (invented products) and visual similarity drops OOD (2410.13232#s1, 2601.22149#s1, 2602.09856#s1).

F.name: Optimistic, sycophantic predictions
F.detail: The world model predicts overly optimistic outcomes that cater to the agent's action, with poor detailed content generation (2602.14721#s1).

F.name: Fidelity scored by an LLM judge from the training family
F.detail: Intrinsic metrics are LLM-judged rather than executed, or the same VLM family serves as RL reward and evaluation judge, which may inflate gains (2601.22149#s1, 2602.14721#s1, 2602.09856#s1).

F.name: No real-environment synthesis baseline or scaling ceiling
F.detail: No comparison against equal-size synthesis in the real environment; gains saturate (~20K rollouts) and taper with data scale; filtering stages and caption quality are not ablated (2602.14721#s2, 2608.05891#s3, 2411.06559#s2, 2604.02345#s1).

S.name: Judge agreement with humans reported
S.detail: The judge is validated against human labels; key-point extraction plus key-screenshot selection keeps agreement over long trajectories (~85-87% with humans) (2504.01382#s1).

S.name: Completion visible in the judged state
S.detail: Tasks are phrased so that completion is visible in a single screenshot or final-state HTML (2406.11896#s2, 2411.02337#s2).

S.name: Graded scores as weights, not hard filters
S.detail: Graded judge scores are used as sampling weights rather than hard filters (2412.19723#s2).

S.name: Judge acquires hidden state actively
S.detail: The verifier escalates from final screenshot to intermediate screenshots to read-only shell/GUI probing of the preserved terminal environment (verifier SR 83.1% vs actor 55.9%) (2602.00575#s1).

S.name: Reliability over coverage via abstention
S.detail: Several judges with different models/prompts, chosen for opposite precision/NPV biases, label only unanimous cases, and their errors are shown to be not fully correlated (2510.18596#s1).

S.name: Human-labelled, in-distribution PRM
S.detail: A process reward model is trained on human step labels from the same environment (94.9% held-out accuracy) (2509.23738#s1).

F.name: Judge sees only partial state
F.detail: Judges see only the last screenshots, so mid-trajectory or hidden-state errors are missed (2412.19723#s2, 2510.18596#s2).

F.name: Disagreement with humans on free-form tasks
F.detail: ~13-20% disagreement with humans; free-form tasks lower precision (2411.02337#s2, 2504.01382#s1, 2406.11896#s2).

F.name: Systematic bias treated as noise
F.detail: Zero-mean reward noise only adds variance, but systematic judge bias is not removed by more rollouts (2605.06732#s3).

F.name: Reward exploitation not analysed
F.detail: Policy exploitation of judge errors / reward hacking and OOD apps are not analysed, often with a single run (2406.11896#s2, 2411.02337#s2, 2509.23738#s1).

F.name: Coverage loss from abstention unvalidated in RL
F.detail: Recall/specificity drop sharply, abstention may bias kept samples, and the ensemble is not validated in an RL loop (2510.18596#s1).

F.name: Generic judge assumed adequate
F.detail: Visual reasoning dominates judge quality; GUI-specialised reward models are no better than base VLMs; a learned PRM stays below oracle reward on offline single-step GRPO (2510.18596#s2, 2509.23738#s3).

S.name: Validated, de-shortcut task set
S.detail: Tasks are validated by humans and shortcuts removed (47% of sampled Mind2Web tasks invalid/outdated; a naive search agent scores 51% vs 22%) (2504.01382#s2).

S.name: Fixed step budget in deterministic resettable apps
S.detail: Agents are compared at a fixed step budget in deterministic, resettable apps (2609.07712#s3).

S.name: Success stratified by reference length with failure audit
S.detail: Success is reported per human reference-length stratum together with efficiency/budget exhaustion and a failure audit (2609.07712#s3, 2504.01382#s2).

S.name: Controlled matched-pair perturbations
S.detail: DOM/VM control is used to inject one controlled change at a time and recompute targets, reporting matched-pair accuracy changes (2604.14262#s1, 2404.07972#s2).

S.name: Closed-loop world-model evaluation with filtered references
S.detail: World models are rolled out autoregressively along reference action sequences and with a probing agent, using reference trajectories filtered for plausibility and state dependence (2609.00048#s3).

F.name: Live-site drift and heterogeneous harnesses
F.detail: Live sites drift, and harnesses and step caps differ across compared agents (2504.01382#s2).

F.name: Aggregate success hides length collapse
F.detail: Success falls monotonically with length for every agent (GPT-5 43.6 -> 14.1%), so an unstratified number hides long-horizon failure (2609.07712#s3).

F.name: Perceptual similarity as world-model fidelity
F.detail: Fine-grained element scores are < 20 while SigLIP is 61-77 and best reference-action progress is 16.7, so global similarity overstates fidelity (2609.00048#s1).

F.name: Single probe agent or same-family judge
F.detail: A single probing agent, a judge from the same model family, and an unvalidated VLM filter are used (2609.00048#s2, 2609.00048#s3).

F.name: Narrow probe sets and training-time randomisation as the fix
F.detail: Perturbation sets are small, web-only and from one model lineage; relational instructions collapse accuracy (UI-TARS-1.5 91.0 -> 35.0) and domain-randomised LoRA SFT does not fix the brittleness (2604.14262#s1, 2604.14262#s2).

S.name: Grounder value shown with a fixed strong planner
S.detail: Holding a strong planner fixed and adding the grounder is reported (o3 23.0 -> 51.0, GPT-4o 5.0 -> 27.0 on OSWorld with Jedi) (2505.13227#s2).

S.name: Screenshot-only grounder at dynamic high resolution
S.detail: The grounder operates on raw screenshots only, trained at dynamic high resolution (2410.05243#s2, 2412.04454#s3).

S.name: Grounding data from rendered structure, mixed and multi-level
S.detail: Exact element boxes are read from rendered DOM/element trees; mixed data types and multiple levels (icon/component/layout) scale without saturation, and web-only data transfers to desktop/mobile (2505.13227#s1, 2410.05243#s1).

S.name: Unified cross-platform action space
S.detail: A unified pyautogui action space is used, packing multiple pairs per screenshot (2412.04454#s1).

S.name: Interface matched to available structure
S.detail: An element-tag interface is used only where a parseable accessibility tree plus OCR exists; an application-specific tool library fits in context (881 tools, 32K) (2410.08164#s3, 2510.17790#s1).

F.name: Planner errors propagate through the NL interface
F.detail: Planning errors (wrong/vague element descriptions) dominate failures and propagate through the natural-language interface; an end-to-end single model is weaker than with a strong external planner (2410.05243#s2, 2505.13227#s2, 2412.04454#s3).

F.name: Ambiguity and refusal unhandled
F.detail: Models rarely refuse; ambiguous instructions cause ~40% of errors (2505.13227#s1, 2412.04454#s1).

F.name: Claims on saturated grounding benchmarks only
F.detail: ScreenSpot v1/v2 saturate and there is an offline-online gap (2501.12326#s3).

F.name: Data returns diminish on long-tail icons
F.detail: Diminishing returns after ~100K screenshots; long-tail and idiosyncratic icons cause grounding errors on mobile/desktop (2410.05243#s1, 2410.05243#s2).

F.name: Interface granularity too coarse
F.detail: Element-ID grounding cannot target sub-element positions (grounding errors in 53% of failures) (2410.08164#s3).

F.name: Tool interface unused by small models
F.detail: Tool gains are modest at 7B (+1.9); small models rarely call tools and make harmful tool calls before RL (2510.17790#s1).

S.name: One-step lookahead horizon
S.detail: The simulated lookahead is one step deep, or the horizon is ablated and H=1 is chosen; H=1 is reported most effective (2411.06559#s1, 2602.09856#s2, 2602.14721#s3).

S.name: Trained, specialised simulator
S.detail: The world model used for lookahead is trained or specialised (abstracted next-state description or code-rendered screen) rather than a naive prompted LLM; an untrained simulator gives much smaller gains (+1.2 vs +9.5 SR on AndroidWorld; prompted 17.5% vs trained 22.0%) (2602.09856#s2, 2410.13232#s2).

S.name: Scorer sees the simulated next state
S.detail: The value model's input includes the predicted next state, and an ablation removing it is reported (SR 22.0 -> 18.0 without it) (2410.13232#s2).

S.name: Verifier accuracy measured and well above chance
S.detail: For direct reranking, the verifier's accuracy is reported and is well above 50%, ideally from a verifier trained on human labels rather than GPT-4o-labelled steps (2602.00575#s2, 2509.23738#s2).

S.name: Non-resettable target and cost stated
S.detail: The paper motivates simulation by an environment that cannot be reset/backtracked and reports cost/latency against tree search (~4-5x lower for simulation); trajectory-level selection keeps terminal state per rollout (2411.06559#s1, 2410.13232#s2, 2602.00575#s2).

F.name: Multi-step simulated rollouts
F.detail: Lookahead uses horizons of 2 or more; multi-step simulation hallucinates actions unavailable in predicted states and compounds error, and horizons 2-3 lose effectiveness (2411.06559#s1, 2410.13232#s2).

F.name: No real-execution search baseline where reset is possible
F.detail: Absolute success remains below real-execution tree search where reset is possible (16.6 vs 19.2 WebArena; 23.6 vs 26.2 VWA); a paper that omits this comparison overstates the move (2410.13232#s2, 2411.06559#s1).

F.name: Gains measured only on short or offline tasks
F.detail: On short MiniWob tasks gains are small (+0.2 to +3.2) and MCTS/hybrid add little; offline SR gains from simulation are ~1.2-1.3 points (2602.14721#s3, 2602.09856#s2).

F.name: Candidate count scaled without compute accounting
F.detail: Best-of-N gains plateau as N grows while compute grows linearly; near-chance verifier accuracy yields negligible or negative Best-of-N gain (2509.23738#s2, 2602.00575#s2).

F.name: Unstable element identity between search and execution
F.detail: Large result-list state spaces (Shopping) shrink gains; element IDs change on reload, causing search/execution mismatch (2410.13232#s2).

S.name: SFT/offline initialisation before online RL
S.detail: Online RL starts from an SFT/offline-trained policy; ~1k online trajectories suffice on short AitW tasks (2406.11896#s1, 2411.02337#s3).

S.name: Constrained updates with success replay
S.detail: Updates are KL-constrained to the previous-phase policy and replay successful trajectories within a perplexity band; tasks are curriculum-filtered for informativeness (2411.02337#s3, 2406.11896#s1).

S.name: First-error correction and recovery data
S.detail: Training data corrects the first erroneous step and adds a recovery action after it; reflection data raises level-2 success 14.58% -> 23.61%, online reflection tuning 23.61% -> 34.72%, and DPO on corrected vs erroneous actions improves OSWorld (72B 18.8 -> 22.7) (2506.08012#s1, 2506.08012#s2, 2501.12326#s1).

S.name: Reasoning kept only if action-consistent
S.detail: Generated per-step thoughts are kept only when the sampled action matches ground truth (bootstrapping), avoiding superficial rationalisation (2501.12326#s2, 2412.04454#s2).

S.name: Offline proxy validated against online success
S.detail: A semi-online/offline protocol is shown to correlate with online success (SOP vs AndroidWorld, R^2=0.934) (2509.11543#s3).

F.name: Unregularised multi-phase updates
F.detail: Without KL or replay, performance degrades over phases; replaying failures destabilises (2411.02337#s3).

F.name: Exact-match correctness rejects valid alternatives
F.detail: Valid alternative actions are treated as mismatches and non-expert branches never see real next states (2509.11543#s1, 2509.11543#s3).

F.name: Short tasks, subsets, few repeats
F.detail: Evaluated on short tasks only, with few repeats and on subsets (WebArena-Lite) (2406.11896#s1, 2411.02337#s3).

F.name: Gains not shown across model sizes
F.detail: Gains shrink with model size (2509.11543#s1).

F.name: Unvalidated error labels and environment assumptions
F.detail: MLLM verifier/first-error labels are not validated against humans, the method assumes Back restores the previous screen, and covers visual/grounding but not high-level planning errors; reflection tuning is not isolated by ablation (2506.08012#s1, 2506.08012#s2, 2501.12326#s1).

F.name: Reasoning noise from source traces
F.detail: Single-sample system-2 decoding is worse in-domain (irrelevant/hallucinated reasoning); redundant actions in source trajectories yield wrong reasoning (7.8%) (2501.12326#s2, 2412.04454#s2).

S.name: Checker reads privileged state
S.detail: Reward comes from reading environment internals (files, configs, backend/localStorage fields, instrumentation flags, logs) compared to goal conditions or gold artefacts (2404.07972#s1, 2601.04126#s2, 2609.07712#s2).

S.name: Outcome-only checks accept alternative paths
S.detail: Checkers test the final state rather than the action sequence, so alternative correct paths are accepted (2404.07972#s1, 2609.07712#s2).

S.name: Tasks synthesised checker-first with test-driven repair
S.detail: Tasks (and generated sites) are produced from an evaluator library or shared spec, with a repair loop until task-relevant tests pass (removing it: 85.6 -> 82.6) (2510.17790#s2, 2601.04126#s1).

S.name: Dense partial credit from instrumented checkpoints
S.detail: Instrumented checkpoints give partial credit and more discriminative RL groups (767 vs 174 discriminative GRPO groups, 4.4x) (2601.04126#s2).

S.name: Difficulty-band filtering before RL
S.detail: Synthesised tasks are filtered to a difficulty band before RL training (2510.17790#s2).

S.name: Two-sided checker validation
S.detail: Checkers/oracles are assessed on independent pools of faulty and legal implementations, measuring false rejects of legal alternatives as well as detection of failures (2610.05001#s2).

F.name: Checker error rates unquantified
F.detail: Residual false positives/negatives are not quantified, and checkpoint weights are LLM-chosen and unvalidated (2404.07972#s1, 2601.04126#s2); two-sided validation remains a survey recommendation, not measured (2610.05001#s2, 2610.05001#s3).

F.name: Manual per-task checkers limit scale
F.detail: Checkers are per-task manual work (~2 man-hours each) and do not exist for unannotated tasks (2404.07972#s1).

F.name: Synthetic environments without real server logic
F.detail: Generated sites have no real server logic and are single-site, single-user in scope (2601.04126#s1).

F.name: Synthesis/test overlap not analysed
F.detail: Overlap between synthesised tasks and the test distribution is not analysed (2510.17790#s2).

F.name: Small downstream RL gain
F.detail: Evaluator-first tasks are harder and fewer, and the RL gain is ~2 points (2510.17790#s2).

F.name: Screenshot-blind state
F.detail: Screenshots alone cannot see some state (e.g. file size), so screenshot judges and scripts are complementary; a design relying on one alone misses cases (2404.07972#s1).
